From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Immediate: ClearStream dedicated pool headroom breach — request for exec bridge

Team —

We're seeing a rapid degradation for ClearStream (CL-2026-183) on their dedicated GPU pool. High-level numbers from the last 45 minutes:
- 95th latency for their text-generation route jumped from ~220ms to ~1.8s for the 8k prompt profile.
- Error rate (5xx + model-timeouts) at ~3.4% (baseline ~0.1%).
- Effective delivered throughput is ~60% of the customer's reserved throughput; backlog queue depth is building.

Attachment: metrics-snapshot-20260611.png (tokenized p95/p99 / error-rate graphs) and clearstream-multiplex.csv (sample request IDs).

Immediate asks:
1) Aditya — can you confirm whether autoscaler failed to provision additional dedicated nodes? Any in-pool noisy neighbor signals or kernel OOMs?
2) Jordan — please prep a short customer note and confirm whether we should propose a short-term credit and an exec bridge.
3) Priyom — raise PagerDuty (if not already) and capture the incident timeline; if this is capacity oversubscription we need to understand burst window and headroom.

Customer is in production for a number of large enterprise customers; ClearStream's SRE just flagged that their customer-facing AI assistants are timing out. This needs exec visibility if we can't stabilize in <2 hours.

I will hold the thread as mailbox owner for customer comms.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Immediate: ClearStream dedicated pool headroom breach — request for exec bridge

Marissa —

Quick triage from infra: I pulled the recent node and serving logs and started an incident page: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-8892. Early signals:
- There's a sustained increase in KV cache churn for the model family ClearStream uses (redwood/gpt-extended-13b), which increased token compute by ~2.1x for 6k+ contexts.
- One dedicated pool rack is showing repeated CUDA context resets and GPU driver watchdog warnings between 08:45–09:40 PT (attached in pd-8892-logs.tgz). Those resets caused the in-pool autoscaler to delay node rebalancing; the autoscaler retry loop hit a quota guard that prevented immediate replacement.
- We also see a surge of long-running requests (customer-side batching) that bypassed our short-request-path optimization and forced larger memory footprints.

Short-term mitigation I recommend (ordered):
1) Failover some traffic to ClearStream's burst capacity in the us-west region (non-dedicated) while we remedy the rack. This keeps latency down but increases unit cost.
2) Temporarily roll traffic to a slightly quantized variant (redwood/gpt-extended-13b-q4_k) for non-SLA-critical tenants in the account to reduce memory pressure.
3) Force drain of the affected GPU host and cordon it from autoscaler until driver stack is patched.

I opened PD-8892 and attached logs (pd-8892-logs.tgz). I can start a remediation window now if leadership approves a brief burst failover. If we trigger failover we'll need Jordan to inform ClearStream and offer compensation.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao

Dalia —

Thank you for the prompt flag. We're treating this as a Sev-1. Summary of current plan (we will open an exec bridge at 17:00 PT):
- Failover: We're initiating a controlled failover of 30% of ClearStream's traffic to burst capacity in us-west as a latency-first mitigation. This should reduce tail latency within 10–15 minutes.
- Replacement: Aditya's team will cordon and drain the affected host, and autoscaler will provision replacements once driver patch is applied.
- Model variant: We'll roll non-SLA routes to a Q4 quantized variant to reduce memory pressure; this will be opt-in for the customer unless we agree otherwise.
- Compensation: Pending root-cause, we can discuss a one-time credit (proposed 10% for the window) now and revisit after RCA.

Exec bridge details (calendar invite to follow):
Time: Thu, Jun 11 17:00 PT
Bridge: Zoom (exec-bridge link in calendar)
Required: Dalia (ClearStream), their CTO or Head of Ops (if available), Aditya (infra lead), Priyom (incident lead), Jordan (customer success), and me.

Attachments: exec-bridge-agenda.pdf (current mitigation timeline + data we will present).

I'll send a customer note right before the bridge confirming the immediate mitigations. If you want to add anything to the agenda please reply to this thread.
